records.subject: A better way to track team projects
records.body:
Hi Ana,

Looking to get more out of Wrenfield? Inviting your teammates is the single biggest thing that makes it click.

Warmly,
Elena Kelly

records.subject: Welcome to Wrenfield, River Ventures!
records.body:
Hi Ana,

Thanks for setting up River Ventures on Wrenfield. If your team is more than one person, inviting them now tends to pay off -- Wrenfield is built around teammates working on shared tasks, not solo lists.

Let me know how the first week goes.

Best,
Nadia Goldberg

records.text: :tada: New signup: *River Ventures* just joined on the starter plan!

decisions.rationale: Day 6, no project, no invite, no key milestone despite three touches (email:4310d2dc, d34909d1, 881112c8). Ana's only reply (email:fe88e783) is a polite deferral with no stated use case or timeline, suggesting low near-term urgency; Starter solo setup lowers odds of self-serve activation in the remaining 8 days.

draft.subject: Re: A few days into Wrenfield — how's it going?
draft.body:
Hi Ana,

Thanks for the update — glad it's gone well so far, and no need for anything urgent on your end.

One thing that tends to make the rest click: projects are the main organizing unit in Wrenfield, and tasks live inside them. If it's useful, I'm happy to walk through creating that first project with you on a short call this week — otherwise the in-app onboarding flow walks through creating a first project whenever you have a few minutes.

Whenever you're ready, a teammate can be invited from Account Settings -> Members at any time.

Best,
Nadia
